caption: A child slides down a plastic playground slide, and at the bottom her hair is standing up from her head.

sa.check: A child on a plastic playground slide.
At the bottom the child's hair is standing up from her head.
The slide is plastic: smooth moulded plastic, not metal.
The hair lies flat or hangs at the top and stands up by the bottom.

pc.expect: The hair rises during or just after the slide and settles slowly afterwards; it does not stand up before the slide begins.
pc.fail: The hair stands up at the top before the child has moved; or rises long after the child has left the slide with nothing near it; or drops flat the instant the slide ends and then rises again; or rises and falls repeatedly at the bottom.

pc.expect: The standing strands stay rooted to the head and fan out; as they settle they fall back onto the head; the child's body follows the slide downward.
pc.fail: Strands detach and float away; or the hair settles upward; or the child rises up the slide without pushing; or the hair stands as a stiff column that stays to the end.

pc.expect: The child moves down the slide along its surface and slows or stops at the bottom.
pc.fail: The child stops half way and starts again with nothing pushing; or leaves the slide's surface and floats down; or moves up the slide; or slides sideways off the chute.

pc.expect: The slide is a rigid plastic chute that keeps its shape under the child; the hair is fine strands.
pc.fail: The slide bends or sags like fabric; or ripples as the child passes; or the hair lifts as one stiff sheet.

pc.expect: One child with the same body, limbs and hair throughout; the child passes through nothing and the slide keeps its shape.
pc.fail: The child gains or loses a limb or changes size; or passes through the slide; or a second child appears from nowhere; or the slide changes shape.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The slide's colour, the child's clothing and the playground stay the same.
pc.fail: The slide changes colour; or the child's clothes change colour; or the playground rearranges.

note: The child is kept because the hair is the physics; the sliding posture is not judged.
